summary: Weekly POC check-in. Customer made progress on VPC peering and KMS provisioning but still needs SSO config and peering CIDR confirmation. Redwood reviewed initial benchmark numbers, suggested quantization + batching tweaks, and agreed next steps around security docs and a full 2-hr load run. Agreed to reconvene next week.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Dr. Aisha Khan: Aisha here.
[00:00:07] Mark Reynolds: Mark on DevOps.
[00:00:09] Priya Singh: Priya, ML eng.
[00:00:11] Carlos Mendes: Carlos from Redwood, SE here.
[00:00:14] Samira Patel: Great. Agenda: onboarding status, access & infra readiness, review preliminary results, tuning suggestions, and action items. We'll keep to 45.
[00:00:28] Mark Reynolds: Quick update from our side: we created the staging VPC and started the peering request to Redwood's shared VPC. We hit a small snag on the CIDR overlap check, so I'm confirming the final ranges today. Also, KMS key provisioning is done but we need instructions for key policies.
[00:00:45] Samira Patel: Perfect — that's the big lift. Carlos, can you remind folks of the KMS key policy we expect?
[00:00:50] Carlos Mendes: Yeah, we need a customer-managed KMS with a policy that allows the Redwood service principal to encrypt/decrypt, plus a read-only rotation role for audit. I can send a sample IAM/KMS policy after. Note — sometimes the sample has the wrong principal name, you know transcription, um I mean, the wrong service principal, so we'll attach the exact one.
[00:01:10] Priya Singh: Thanks, that will help. On the model side, we ran three test batches against the hosted endpoint yesterday — small set, 100 requests each. Latency medians were around 230ms for the default model and 470ms for the 2x-longer context runs. Token cost looked roughly in-line with your estimate but we didn't test sustained throughput.
[00:01:30] Carlos Mendes: Okay that's good signals. Can you paste the raw results in the spreadsheet? We'll be able to map those to batching/quantization profiles.
[00:01:35] Priya Singh: Will do.
[00:01:36] Samira Patel: On the peering: Mark, once you confirm the CIDR I'll pass it to infra to push the peering. Any blockers on firewall/NAT rules?
[00:01:45] Mark Reynolds: We need to open outbound 443 to the Redwood egress IPs, but we're waiting on the exact IP list.
[00:01:51] Samira Patel: I'll attach the current egress list in the slack thread and include it in the network doc.
[00:01:57] Dr. Aisha Khan: On compliance, our legal asked for SOC 2 plus an architecture diagram for auditors.
[00:02:03] Samira Patel: We have a SOC2 pack; I'll send that after the call. We'll include the architecture diagram and a brief on how data is isolated in Dedicated vs Hosted.
[00:02:12] Carlos Mendes: Quick note on the isolation: for Dedicated we map a single-tenant GPU pool to your tenant, so KV cache and model weights don't cross tenants. For Hosted we still isolate data at the tenant layer but there are shared infra components. I think the legal team wanted that language clarified, right?
[00:02:27] Dr. Aisha Khan: Yes, exact wording is important.
[00:02:29] Samira Patel: We'll make sure wording is explicit.
[00:02:32] [00:02:32] Priya Singh: About the results review, we saw a tail variance on the long-context runs. I suspect the KV cache isn't being warmed correctly for our prefix-heavy workflow — many queries reuse a 512-token prefix.
[00:02:45] Carlos Mendes: That makes sense. Our runtime uses prefix/KV caching heuristics; if you're reusing the same prefix we can pin that to the cache and speed warmups. Two levers: 1) explicit prefix caching via the SDK, 2) increase in-memory KV allocation on the Dedicated pool. Both have cost/latency implications.
[00:03:02] Samira Patel: Priya, are you on Dedicated or Hosted for the pilot?
[00:03:05] Priya Singh: We're on Hosted for the initial pilot, planned to move to Dedicated if numbers check out.
[00:03:10] Carlos Mendes: For Hosted we can still do prefix caching client-side; we can also recommend batching groups by prefix to increase cache hits. Another approach is to move to a quantized model variant to reduce per-token time — 4-bit quant gives lower memory but sometimes increases occasional decoding jitter, so it's a trade.
[00:03:27] Mark Reynolds: Can you quantify the trade? Like percent speedup for 4-bit quant vs accuracy/quality regression?
[00:03:33] Carlos Mendes: Rough ballpark: 4-bit quant often reduces memory footprint by ~2.5-3x and can reduce inference latency per token by 15-25% on our tested kernels. Quality regressions are model and prompt dependent — we recommend A/B evals on your prompt-set. We'll provide per-model QA numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[00:03:52] Samira Patel: We're going to add per-prompt evals to the sheet. Priya, can you flag the top 30 prompts for Nexa's use case?
[00:03:59] Priya Singh: Yep, I'll export those and share by Friday.
[00:04:02] [00:04:02] Dr. Aisha Khan: Also a question on SSO. We're SAML-based, need a SAML flow and group mapping for RBAC. What's the timeline?
[00:04:11] Samira Patel: We support SAML SSO. I have the SSO setup guide, but our security team prefers to run a test with a single admin user first. Should be quick — couple hours to configure and test.
[00:04:21] Carlos Mendes: Note: when you map groups, you can tie group names to roles in the Redwood Console so your auditors get consistent RBAC logs. We'll provide the sample attribute mapping.
[00:04:29] Mark Reynolds: Good — that helps.
[00:04:31] Priya Singh: On environment readiness for load testing, Mark and I can run a 2-hour sustained run at 200 rps against staging next week if we get the service account + key.
[00:04:42] Samira Patel: We'll provision a service account and short-lived key for staging access. Expect a note from me tonight.
[00:04:48] Mark Reynolds: About monitoring — do you ship logs to our Splunk or do we pull from your console?
[00:04:53] Carlos Mendes: We have push and pull options. For POC we usually enable syslog forwarding and give a read-only API token for pulling traces. If you want long-term ingestion to Splunk we'll coordinate with your infra team and provide HEC endpoint examples.
[00:05:06] Dr. Aisha Khan: Any thoughts on cost controls for the pilot? We want guardrails so it doesn't spike unexpectedly.
[00:05:12] Samira Patel: Yes, we can set per-route quotas, rate limits, and alerts for spend thresholds. We'll preconfigure a monthly cap for the pilot and send alerts at 50/75/90%. Also, usage dashboards are in the Console.
[00:05:24] Priya Singh: For the tuning part, Carlos, you mentioned batching. What's a good starting batch size for our median 512-token context?
[00:05:32] Carlos Mendes: Start with a batch size of 8-16 for 512-token median; it increases throughput but can increase tail latency. If your SLA is 400ms p99 we err on smaller batch sizes. We'll put recommended profiles: low-latency (batch 4), balanced (8), cost-optimized (16+ with async).
[00:05:49] Samira Patel: We're going to include those three profiles in the benchmark sheet.
[00:05:53] [00:05:53] Priya Singh: One more question — how are tokenization differences handled? We saw slight token count differences between models.
[00:06:00] Carlos Mendes: Good catch. Different model families have different tokenizers; we normalize by reporting token counts per model for the same prompt in the sheet, and recommend a model mapping.
[00:06:10] Dr. Aisha Khan: This is great — we're almost ready to run the bigger load test once the peering and test creds are in place.
[00:06:17] Samira Patel: Recap of immediate blockers: Mark to confirm CIDR (due 6/10), Samira to send SOC2 & network diagram (6/11), Carlos to update benchmark sheet with quantization and batching profiles (6/14), Priya to run 2-hr load test (6/15). Anything else?
[00:06:32] Mark Reynolds: I will also check firewall rules and share the egress exceptions.
[00:06:35] Priya Singh: I'll add the top 30 prompts.
[00:06:37] Dr. Aisha Khan: Legal wants the clear Dedicated vs Hosted wording in the doc, so please include that.
[00:06:42] Samira Patel: We'll add a short paragraph called 'isolation and compliance' to the pack.
[00:06:46] [00:06:46] Carlos Mendes: Quick technical note — during the load run please include an option to capture KV cache hit/miss metrics. That will tell us if prefix caching is working. If miss rate >20% we'll tweak caching strategy.
[00:06:58] Mark Reynolds: Will do.
[00:07:00] Samira Patel: Okay, schedule — same time next week? 14:00 PT on 2027-06-16?
[00:07:06] Dr. Aisha Khan: Works for us.
[00:07:08] Mark Reynolds: Confirmed.
[00:07:10] Priya Singh: Confirmed.
[00:07:12] Samira Patel: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the docs and the egress IPs.
[00:07:19] [00:07:19] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some slight ASR errors in product names (e.g., K-V cache vs KV cache, SAM-el for SAML in one auto-notes) — cleaned marginally in summary but original transcript lines preserved as spoken.
